History of Present Illness:
35-year-old woman. Eighteen hours of epigastric pain that became concentrated under the right ribs and radiates to the right shoulder. No diarrhea.

Physical Examination:
Focal right upper-quadrant tenderness with inspiratory arrest on palpation. Temperature 38.0 C; heart rate 100/min; BP 128/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 22/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 14.0 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 234 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 63 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 34 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 52 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 45 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 89 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)
Serum pregnancy test: negative (reference negative)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: immobile stone in the gallbladder neck, wall thickening to 4.5 mm and surrounding fluid; ducts are not dilated.
